learning: Iteration 10 confirmed that midpoint inertia (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16) on the 0.12 track removes slalom line loss while improving oval progress. max_error stayed near 0.062 m across every geometry and gain, so it appears to track the run-ending threshold rather than a tuning target.
notes: Final package: the iteration-10 geometry and iteration-10 controller, delivered unchanged. This is the best-measured design (146.27), so no untested change is added before the unseen-track race.
rationale: The Builder's final geometry is the iteration-10 platform, unchanged: five sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.16, mass 0.75. Iteration 10 raced this exact geometry with the controller below and scored 146.27, the best of the run. Its development results were oval progress 0.597 with 3 of 20 runs finishing, slalom line loss 0.0 and s-bend progress 0.146 with no line loss. The controller that produced that result is the iteration-10 controller (kp 3.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, weights -2 to +2, last_direction). I am delivering it unchanged. Every controller change tried on the 0.12 platform either raised line loss or was confounded with a geometry change, and max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.066 m across all geometries and gains, so no measured lever points to a better gain set. This is the final iteration, so an untested gain change would add risk to the unseen-track race, which is scored on whatever is delivered. The best-measured design is the safest choice.
